name: Wooden Tserkvas of the Carpathian Region in Poland and Ukraine
description: Sixteen log-built churches are scattered across the Carpathian foothills of southeastern Poland and western Ukraine. Raised between the 16th and 19th centuries by Orthodox and Greek Catholic villagers, each has three sections topped with shingled domes and cupolas. Inside, painted walls and carved iconostasis screens glow in the dim light, and some churches still have their own wooden bell towers and graveyards.
